newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent down as paper curve heads into contang.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent down as paper curve heads into contang.

text.p: North Sea Brent weakened further on Thursday on the cash and physical market as the front end of the Brent curve headed back into contango, traders said.
No Brent physical deals were reported and traders said the benchmark crude was thinly talked at about June Brent -25 cents, roughly the same distressed level a May 23-35 cargo traded at on Wednesday.
On the cash market, June Brent, which expires at the end of Thursday's session, was trading 11 cents down at $19.40 by 1744 GMT.
Traders said Brent crude was pushed down by the fact that the June loading programme for the Brent system came out just a little lower than May's.
"No one is very anxious to buy," one European trader said, adding that a "quite normal" June loading programme was keeping buyers in a wait-and-see mode.

Brent system operator Shell Exploration and Production (Shell Expro) on Thursday estimated Brent crude system throughput in June at 408,806 barrels per day (bpd), a little down from 409,045 bpd in May.
Traders said they were waiting for the Forties June programme to be released on Friday and expected it to be a little weaker than last month due to maintenance work.
Another factor that stressed Brent were signs that a recent narrowing of refining margins were prompting refiners towards cutting crude througput, traders said.
Traders said that the futures contract was pushed down partly by news that Texaco had cut crude throughput at a refinery in Rotterdam.
"The IPE seems to be in contango now," one paper trader said.
